why_this_tool: Backstage puts the catalog, software templates, TechDocs and a plugin model in one open source portal that runs on a laptop, so every part of turning a one-off customer build into a reusable paved path can be practised in one place.
alternatives: Port and Cortex are hosted developer portals that trade plugin-level control for less operational work; Cookiecutter scaffolds repos without a catalog or portal; LaunchDarkly, Unleash and OpenFeature provide runtime feature flags that Backstage does not; Terraform modules and Helm charts package reusable infrastructure rather than a paved path for developers.

setup.why: This gives you a working portal with the catalog, templates and TechDocs already wired in, which every later step customizes.

steps.why: The catalog is the centre of the portal, and you need to see what a registered piece of software looks like before modelling your own customer work.

steps.do: Write a catalog descriptor file for one past customer build and register it in the catalog by its repository location.
steps.done_when: Your customer build appears in the catalog list with the name and description you wrote.

source.title: Backstage Software Catalog | Backstage Software Catalog and Developer Platform

steps.why: A one-off build that is not in the catalog is invisible to the next engagement. Registering it is the first step toward reuse.

steps.do: Create Group entities for a field team and a platform team, then model the build as a Component in a System with an API, with each part owned by the right group.
steps.done_when: The component page shows the platform team as owner of the shared API and the field team as owner of the customer component, with the relation graph linking them.

source.title: Technical overview | Backstage Software Catalog and Developer Platform

steps.why: Platform as a product only works when ownership and the interface between field and platform teams are explicit. The system model is how Backstage records who provides what to whom.

steps.do: Write a generalization decision for three pieces of the customer build, placing each in the app, a plugin package or a common package using the code placement guidance.
steps.done_when: You have a three-row note naming each piece, its chosen package location and the reason, and at least one piece is deliberately left customer-specific.

steps.why: Deciding what to generalize is a judgement about how many consumers a piece has. The package architecture gives concrete homes for customer-specific, shared and cross-cutting code.

steps.do: Compare the Backstage release your app installed against the latest release notes and list the breaking changes that touch your catalog, templates and TechDocs.
steps.done_when: You have a written list of the breaking changes that apply to your app and the upgrade action for each.

steps.why: Shared tooling only stays reusable if it survives upgrades, so you need the habit of checking what changed between the version you have and the current one.

steps.do: Run a software template from the Create page to scaffold a new service from the pattern in your customer build, and follow the task log to completion.
steps.done_when: The task finishes with all steps green, a new repository exists in your test account, and the new component is registered in the catalog.

steps.why: A template is the golden path itself: it turns the repeated first week of an engagement into a form anyone on the field team can fill in.

steps.do: Write a short documentation site next to the scaffolded component's code and view it rendered in the component's docs tab through TechDocs.
steps.done_when: The Docs tab of your component renders your pages, and they also appear in the portal's documentation list.

source.title: TechDocs Documentation | Backstage Software Catalog and Developer Platform

steps.why: A paved path nobody can find instructions for does not get used. Docs kept beside the code stay current with the template.

steps.done_when: Starting the app with customer A's overlay and then customer B's shows different titles and catalog contents from the same code.

steps.why: This is the toggle pattern at the portal level: one codebase and a small overlay per customer, instead of a fork per customer. Backstage has no runtime flag service, so config layering is the closest built-in equivalent.

steps.do: Configure scaffolder template filtering so that each customer overlay shows only the templates meant for that customer or team.
steps.done_when: The Create page shows a different set of templates under each customer configuration.

source.title: v1.55.0 | Backstage Software Catalog and Developer Platform

steps.why: Per-customer variation applies to golden paths too. Filtering lets one template library serve many engagements without exposing the wrong path.

steps.do: Package one field customization as its own plugin package in the monorepo, with a pinned version, and install it into the app from that package.
steps.done_when: A clean checkout followed by a locked install and a build produces the app with your plugin loaded, with no manual edits.

source.title: Architecture overview | Backstage Software Catalog and Developer Platform

steps.why: A customization that lives in a named, versioned package can be reproduced in the next deployment and built by any pipeline. Code pasted into the app cannot.

steps.do: Configure the backend to use PostgreSQL and a Redis cache running in local containers in place of the in-memory defaults.
steps.done_when: After a backend restart your registered components are still present, and the backend log shows connections to PostgreSQL and Redis.

source.title: Architecture overview | Backstage Software Catalog and Developer Platform

steps.why: The in-memory database loses the catalog on every restart. A real database and cache are the minimum for a portal that several engagements share.

steps.do: Configure sign-in and restrict who can register catalog entities and run templates, working through the operator responsibilities in the threat model.
steps.done_when: Guest access is off, a signed-in test user can run only the allowed templates, and you have a checklist marking each operator responsibility as met or open.

source.title: Backstage Threat Model | Backstage Software Catalog and Developer Platform

steps.why: Templates execute actions with the portal's credentials and catalog input is partly untrusted. A portal shared between field and platform teams must be locked down before it carries customer work.
